source.title: JTok: On Token Embedding as another Axis of Scaling Law via Joint Token Self-modulation
source.authors: Ye-Bin Yang; Huai-Jin Wu; Fu-Ming Guo; Lin-Li Yao; Xiao-Han Qin; Jing-Zhi Wang; Debing Zhang; Jun-Chi Yan

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior for a new setting: token-indexed parameters added to MoE language models, including an isoFLOPs analysis and a held-out-loss capacity sweep.
record.gate_note: Direct evidence for V1 is the held-out test-loss isoFLOPs data and the held-out-loss sweep over JTok-M capacity. The paper describes isoFLOPs minima but does not report how the minimizing backbone parameter count and token count vary with compute. Training-loss trajectories, downstream benchmark scores, and efficiency results do not directly test the listed versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own isoFLOPs sweeps on MoE language models over five budgets (3e18–3e20 FLOPs). It fits the compute-optimal held-out test loss as a power law in compute. It also sweeps token-indexed (JTok-M) parameter count at a fixed backbone and measures held-out loss. Both bear on V1 in a new setting: MoE, plus a FLOP-free parameter type.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that token-indexed parameters are a complementary scaling axis. JTok-M shifts the MoE compute-optimal frontier down by a constant factor (about 2.2% lower loss, 35% compute saving), which they claim is scale-invariant. JTok-M capacity follows a log-linear trend that they call a predictable power law.
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out loss and an isoFLOPs procedure with quadratic fits around minima, but tests MoE backbones augmented with token-indexed JTok-M parameters rather than the original dense-model parameter/data sweeps. The additional JTok-M capacity is also swept at fixed backbone and token count.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported JTok-M capacity trend is measured at fixed 3.9B-A0.6B backbone, 100B tokens, and ρ = 0.25; the compute-frontier comparison uses fixed η = 50 and ρ = 0.25.
record.problems: Only five compute-budget points are reported for the frontier fits, with no error bars or confidence intervals. The optimal-loss analysis does not report the optimal parameter/token allocations themselves. The capacity-sweep curve is described as approximately log-linear, but detailed numerical points are not tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss trajectories in Figure 2 and Figure 7 are not held-out-loss scaling results. Downstream benchmark scores and system throughput results do not measure a listed version. No qualifying held-out-loss scaling rows were otherwise omitted.

untested.parts: Parameter and token scaling of dense models with the other factors non-bottlenecked. The compute frontier spans only 2 orders of magnitude. The token-indexed parameter sweep spans under 1 order.
No fit on small runs used to predict much larger runs.
Nc*(C) and D*(C) are estimated but not reported or fitted against compute.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
Downstream gains are reported but not related to scale or loss predictively.
One fitting procedure only. No test of fitting choices or curvature.

missing.what: Per-budget isoFLOPs curve points and the loss-optimal Nc*(C), D*(C) obtained from the quadratic fits. These are needed to check V3 allocation exponents and are not reported numerically.
Final loss for three backbone sizes (2.3B-A0.5B, 3.9B-A0.6B, 9.8B-A1.4B) at 100B tokens. Only the JTok-M deltas (0.059, 0.064, 0.051) are given; the plotted loss appears to be a training curve.
Data points of the η sweep. Only the slope per doubling is stated.

record.verdict_notes: The fitted slope is log2 L per log10 C (−0.2016), which corresponds to L ∝ C^−0.061. Kaplan excluded embedding parameters from N. Treating token-indexed (embedding-like, FLOP-free) parameters as a V1 parameter axis is therefore an extension, and the sweep is too short to establish a power law. JTok-M frontier points reuse vanilla-optimal backbones, so they are not true JTok-M optima. No uncertainty is reported. The 35% saving rests on an intercept difference of about 0.045 between fits.

versions.untested_parts: Tests held-out loss against JTok-M capacity and compute-optimal loss against compute in MoE settings. Does not separately test conventional dense model parameter count or training-token scaling with the other factors held non-bottleneck.
No test of fitting on small runs and predicting held-out runs orders of magnitude larger.
Although isoFLOPs minima are used to obtain optimal losses, the paper does not report the optimal backbone parameter counts and token counts across budgets or fit their growth with compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Experiments concern text pretraining; no other modalities, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law test.
Downstream benchmarks are reported, but the paper does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
The study reports one fitting procedure and setup; it does not vary fitting choices or demonstrate disagreement or bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: 3.9B-A0.6B +JTok-M
rows.operation_detail: Swept JTok-M parameter expansion ratio while holding the backbone specification and other training hyperparameters fixed; measured held-out loss.
rows.measure: Held-out loss as JTok-M parameter capacity increases
rows.value: Monotonic loss reduction; approximately 0.0118 loss reduction per doubling of JTok-M parameters
rows.note: The paper describes the trend as approximately log-linear; Figure 6b plots the curve.
rows.check: η spans only 30–130, under one order of magnitude. Figure 6b shows loss moving only about 2.045→2.025. The trend is described as linear in log η (a fixed loss drop per doubling), which over this range cannot be told apart from a power law. No numerical points are tabulated.

relationships.reason: Compute-optimal held-out loss falls from 2.654 to 2.018 across five budgets. The log-log fit has R2=0.9994 (r1, r3, r5, r7, r9, r11).
relationships.display_finding: Held-out loss falls from 2.654 to 2.018 across five compute budgets, with a log-log fit achieving R²=0.9994.

relationships.condition: JTok-M-augmented MoE frontier (η=50, ρ=0.25), same budgets
relationships.reason: Loss falls from 2.598 to 1.973. The log-log fit has R2=0.9991, with slope matching vanilla (−0.2009 vs −0.2016) (r2, r4, r6, r8, r10, r12).
relationships.display_finding: Loss falls from 2.598 to 1.973 with R²=0.9991 and slope −0.2009, close to vanilla's −0.2016.

relationships.condition: Token-indexed parameter sweep, 3.9B-A0.6B backbone, 100B tokens, η 30–130
relationships.reason: Held-out loss falls monotonically, about 0.0118 per doubling of JTok-M parameters. The range is narrow, under one order of magnitude (r13).
relationships.display_finding: Held-out loss decreases monotonically by about 0.0118 per doubling of JTok-M parameters over less than one order of magnitude.
